resources.string: Cloudy stream qualification
Native streaming engine qualification

Real Moonlight native loading and app-owned client identity qualification. Explicit pairing uses a private loopback fixture; a separate explicit preview uses a pinned LAN host and the real video/audio engine. Local device credentials are entered only in the system prompt.
Load native engine

Close diagnostic
App-owned client identity

Create a separate non-exportable RSA client identity for this diagnostic. Approve with your device credential or a strong biometric. A successful local signature does not qualify TLS, pairing or the product vault. Pending enrollment can be completed after a new approval. Nothing connects automatically.
Ready to inspect the local identity.

Delete this identity
Delete only this diagnostic’s local identity and pending keys? Its public operation journal remains. Any future enrolled host would need separate revocation and deliberate re-enrollment.
Authorize diagnostic client identity
Allow this local certificate and signing check. No host connection will be opened.
The local native operation was cancelled. Its worker has retired; inspect the retained record for any completed observation.
Authorize with screen-lock credential
Use the screen-lock PIN, pattern or password for this local signing check. The existing key policy is unchanged.

Finite pairing with the existing READY identity only. Provision no_backup/pairing-config.json with the approved public certificate, exact pin and 127.0.0.1 HTTP/HTTPS ports forwarded to the isolated fixture. Enter its four-digit pairing PIN here, then approve a fresh screen-lock prompt. The 30-second authorization includes signing, real pairing and one client-certificate HTTPS application-list read. No automatic retry, unpair or playback occurs. Cancellation can leave host enrollment intact.
Memory-only four-digit host pairing PIN
Pair with fixture using screen-lock credential
Request local network permission
Authorize this finite loopback pairing and client-certificate HTTPS read with the existing identity.
Real pairing and client-certificate HTTPS application-list read completed. No video was decoded.
Finite native playback preview

Read the real paired HTTPS application catalog from privately provisioned no_backup/catalog-config.json, then select a returned application ID. A separate fresh screen-lock approval starts at most 30 seconds of real 1280 × 720 H.264 SDR video and audio, including setup. No guessed ID or old playback-config fallback is used. No automatic pairing, retry or replacement of another host application occurs. Input forwarding is not part of this preview. One native playback run is allowed per process; restart the diagnostic for another. Cancellation may leave the host application running.
No playback observation yet. Decoder submissions, buffers released for rendering and actual frame-render callbacks are separate counters; none alone proves visible presentation or latency.
Authorize and start finite playback
Native video preview surface
Authorize this selected pinned LAN application preview with the existing identity. The entire attempt shares this approval’s 30-second window.
Retry pending local playback cleanup
Playback ownership is retained until the worker, native cleanup, surface handoff and terminal evidence are confirmed.
The engine retired. Waiting for the actual preview surface destruction callback before release.
Playback retired and its surface was released. Inspect the actual counters and retained terminal record.
Reconcile previous process evidence…
Acknowledge local interruption

Acknowledge only well-formed unfinished records from a previous diagnostic process. Original records remain unchanged and host state remains UNKNOWN. This performs no network operation, retry, unpair or host stop. Malformed evidence requires deliberate private-file repair.
Previous process interruption acknowledged in a separate verified receipt. Host state remains UNKNOWN; no network action was replayed.

Explicit paired application discovery uses only pinned HTTPS /applist on the approved numeric LAN peer. Provision no_backup/catalog-config.json with schema 1, profile ID, numeric address, HTTP/HTTPS/RTSP ports, SHA-256 certificate pin and public certificate DER Base64. No application ID belongs in that file. A fresh screen-lock approval qualifies the existing READY identity. Reading does not pair, launch or consume the one-native-playback allowance. Catalog titles and selection remain in memory only; preview requires another fresh approval.
